title: Align two eigenvalues in one geometric simple constituent before choosing a curve
statement: Let $k_0$ be a finite field and $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k_0$. Let $X$ be smooth affine of finite type over $k_0$. In the source pro-etale Weil category [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], let $G$ be lisse [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], and let $G_1\hookrightarrow G_2\hookrightarrow G$ be a lisse subquotient diagram with irreducible nonzero lisse quotient $V$. For two closed points $x,y$ and local Frobenius eigenvalues $\alpha,\beta$ of $V$ [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], there exist a finite extension $k_1/k_0$, a smooth geometrically connected separated affine finite-type $k_1$-scheme $Y$ of constant relative dimension $d>0$, and lisse $F_1\hookrightarrow F_2\hookrightarrow F$ with geometrically irreducible quotient $S=\operatorname{coker}(F_1\to F_2)$. There are closed $x_1,y_1$ of $Y$, integers $e,f>0$, and a morphism $p:Y\to X$ with $p(x_1)=x$, $p(y_1)=y$ and $p\gg p_X=p_Y\gg\operatorname{Spec}(k_0\to k_1)$, such that $q_{x_1}=q_x^e$, $q_{y_1}=q_y^f$, and $\alpha^e,\beta^f$ are eigenvalues of $S$ at $x_1,y_1$. For every coefficient embedding $\iota$, reality [def-wf-iota-real] of $G$ implies reality of $F$. Geometric irreducibility means that the underlying pro-etale lisse sheaf is nonzero and every lisse subobject is zero or the whole object. There is no assertion that $Y$ is a curve. A dimension-zero supporting component is replaced by its affine line; empty bases and zero quotients cannot satisfy the eigenvalue assumptions.

proof.text: Apply the geometric constituent orbit decomposition to the irreducible cokernel. Each given eigenvalue supplies a nonzero stalk, so its hypotheses hold. This supplies the exact functor R, geometry, point lifts, powers, reality, and the direct sum.

proof.text: Transport each powered eigenvalue across the characteristic-polynomial identity. Under the stalk map of the direct-sum isomorphism take a nonzero eigenvector. The sum of inclusion-projection maps is the identity, so some projection is nonzero; it is an eigenvector in that summand because stalk maps commute with Frobenius. Choose a summand for alpha at s and a summand for beta at t. The orbit point transport moves the beta summand to the alpha summand at a new lift t prime with unchanged residue cardinality.

proof.text: The inclusion of the selected summand into R(cokernel i) gives a monomorphism into cokernel(R(i)) by exactness. Pull back this inclusion along the cokernel projection. The original source R(G1) is the kernel of the pullback projection, which is epi, so its cokernel is the selected summand. The pullback embeds into R(G2), hence into R(G). It is lisse as the kernel of the difference map from the biproduct of two lisse sheaves into the lisse cokernel. Transport geometric irreducibility and both eigenvalues across the resulting cokernel isomorphism and assemble the witnesses.

theorem exists_pair_eigenvalue_geometric_constituent
    {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime]
    [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [IsAffine X]
    [Smooth (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    {G : WeilSheaf k₀ l X} (hG : G.IsLisse) {G₁ G₂ : WeilSheaf k₀ l X}
    (i : G₁ ⟶ G₂) (j : G₂ ⟶ G) [Mono i] [Mono j]
    (h₁ : G₁.IsLisse) (h₂ : G₂.IsLisse)
    (hirr : (cokernel i).IsIrreducibleLisse)
    (x y : X.finitePoints) (α β : PadicAlgCl l)
    (hα : ((cokernel i).stalk x).frobeniusEnd.HasEigenvalue α)
    (hβ : ((cokernel i).stalk y).frobeniusEnd.HasEigenvalue β) :
    ∃ (k₁ : Type u) (_ : Field k₁) (_ : Finite k₁) (_ : Algebra k₀ k₁)
      (_ : Fact (ringChar k₁ ≠ l)) (d : ℕ) (C : Scheme.{u})
      (_ : C.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁))) (_ : IsAffine C)
      (_ : SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : GeometricallyConnected (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : IsSeparated (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : LocallyOfFiniteType (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : QuasiCompact (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (H H₁ H₂ : WeilSheaf k₁ l C) (a : H₁ ⟶ H₂) (b : H₂ ⟶ H)
      (_ : Mono a) (_ : Mono b),
      H.IsLisse ∧ H₁.IsLisse ∧ H₂.IsLisse ∧ (cokernel a).IsGeometricallyIrreducible ∧ 0 < d ∧
      (∀ ι : PadicAlgCl l →+* ℂ, G.IsReal ι → H.IsReal ι) ∧
      ∃ (s t : C.finitePoints) (e f : ℕ), 0 < e ∧ 0 < f ∧
        (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)).residueCard s.1 =
          (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)).residueCard x.1 ^ e ∧
        (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)).residueCard t.1 =
          (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)).residueCard y.1 ^ f ∧
        ((cokernel a).stalk s).frobeniusEnd.HasEigenvalue (α ^ e) ∧
        ((cokernel a).stalk t).frobeniusEnd.HasEigenvalue (β ^ f) ∧
        ∃ c : C ⟶ X,
          c ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)) =
            (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)) ≫
              Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k₀ k₁)) ∧
          c s.1 = x.1 ∧ c t.1 = y.1
